concepts.label: XDCR (Couchbase Server)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - this is the Web Console procedure-guide's own top-level overview of the promoted server:xdcr concept.

concepts.label: XDCR Reference (registered target cluster)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the registration, on the local cluster, of a remote target cluster for XDCR. Named here only in passing ('Reference management: Remote clusters must be registered as targets for XDCR'); the full definition is minted on create-xdcr-reference.md, this batch's own defining page for the concept. First contact anywhere in the corpus - the xdcr-reference/ reference tree (round 20) never needed to name this object, since it documents filtering/settings mechanisms rather than the reference-registration step itself.

concepts.label: XDCR Replication
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the continuously-running replication object created between a source and target bucket. Named here only in passing ('Replication management: Once a reference has been registered...it can be specified as the target for a replication'); the full definition is minted on create-xdcr-replication.md. First contact anywhere in the corpus - Capella's own xdcr.json/manage-xdcr-replications.json (round 7) used the umbrella capella:xdcr concept plus xdcr:replication-filter/xdcr:replication-status-enum, but never minted a concept for the replication object itself.

concepts.label: vBucket
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - promoted (aliases to concepts/server/vbucket.json). This page uses vBucket count equality as an XDCR precondition.

relations.subject: server:xdcr
relations.evidence: Couchbase has modified the license restrictions to its Couchbase Server Community Edition package, for version 7.0 and higher: in consequence, XDCR is promoted to a commercial-only feature of Enterprise Edition.

relations.subject: server:xdcr
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (availableSince) - marks when the Enterprise-only gate took effect, not when XDCR itself was introduced
relations.evidence: Couchbase has modified the license restrictions to its Couchbase Server Community Edition package, for version 7.0 and higher: in consequence, XDCR is promoted to a commercial-only feature of Enterprise Edition.

relations.subject: server:xdcr
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (requiresCapability) - loose fit: object is an equal-count precondition on a structural artifact, not a bucket/storage/edition capability, matching this project's precedent of loose predicate reuse over minting a near-duplicate
relations.evidence: Note that XDCR can only be established between clusters whose numbers of vBuckets are equal: all supported platforms have _1024_ vBuckets except _MacOS_, which has _64_.

relations.subject: xdcr:replication

relations.evidence: Once a reference has been registered on the local cluster, it can be specified as the target for a _replication_.

notable_absence.finding: This overview page tells the reader to 'make sure that you have appropriate permissions for managing XDCR' but names no specific role - it defers entirely to prepare-for-xdcr.md, this batch's own next page, for the Full/Cluster/XDCR Administrator triple.

cross_component_finding: CONFIRMS THIS BATCH'S REUSE-DENSITY HYPOTHESIS AT THE TOP LEVEL: the overview page's own task list (Preparation, Reference management, Replication management, Pausing/Resuming, Recovering Data) maps one-to-one onto this batch's 16 page titles, and every substantive XDCR mechanism it gestures at (filtering, advanced settings, scopes/collections) already has a promoted or extraction-layer xdcr:* id from round 7 (Capella) or round 20 (server/8.0/xdcr-reference/). The two genuinely new ids this page's own text forces into existence - xdcr:reference and xdcr:replication - are structural/procedural nouns for the objects these UI actions create, not new XDCR mechanisms; the reference tree and Capella's overview page both talked ABOUT replication filtering/settings without ever needing to name the reference-registration or replication-object level themselves, because neither of those trees is a step-by-step creation procedure.
